what_they_do: Trace is an AI orchestration platform that connects to a company's existing tools (Slack, Notion, Jira, Google Drive, HubSpot) and builds a persistent model of how work moves between departments. It deploys AI agents to handle parts of a task and routes the parts that need judgment to the right human, replacing the manual handoffs and status-chasing that normally happen across tools during things like client onboarding, contract review, and financial approvals.
theme_fit_rationale: Trace explicitly sits between departments and existing systems, coordinating AI agents and humans across a multi-step, multi-tool workflow (onboarding, contract review, financial approvals) rather than serving one narrow vertical. That is a direct match to Theme 2 (agents executing cross-functional, multi-system workflows), including the read/write-across-systems and human+agent coordination framing. No strong secondary theme fits; it is not vertical-specific enough for Theme 5 and is not agent-facing infrastructure (Theme 3), it IS the agent layer.

Hey Tim - Know I've reached out a couple times but wanted to see if now is a better time. I help lead our enterprise AI investing at Telescope, a $275M Series A fund started by a former Sequoia partner. We lead $5-30M Series A investments in a handful of exceptional companies each year.

As we've continued to think about enterprise AI, we've continued to see that most workflow products start too small. They automate an individual task, but lose the context as soon as work crosses from one team or agent to another. Trace is building around that handoff itself, carrying the state of the business forward and deciding what can run autonomously, what needs human judgment, and what has to be checked before the process moves on. If that layer works, the individual agents become interchangeable and Trace becomes the system coordinating how the company actually operates.
